blocks.text: Bolivar Heights Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Bolivar Heights is a North Surrey neighbourhood inside the City of Surrey's City Centre Plan area, north of the City Centre core.
Two City parks mark the area's extent: Bolivar Park at 13591 Crestview Drive and Invergarry Park at 11285 Surrey Road.

blocks.text: Bolivar Heights Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Bolivar Heights houses sit inside a plan area the City is now steering toward growth, including a mixed-use neighbourhood centre, while the surrounding City Centre takes high-density residential and mixed-use development.
The two public elementary schools physically in the area are James Ardiel Elementary at 13751 112 Avenue and Surrey Traditional School at 13875 113 Avenue.

blocks.text: Bolivar Heights Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The City Centre Plan update now underway allows for growth in the Bolivar Heights area, including a mixed-use neighbourhood centre, so a house lot's future land use here is set by that update, not only by its current zoning.

Lots near the Bon Accord ravine in Invergarry Park adjoin protected riparian creek habitat, and Surrey may require a development permit in its Steep Slope and Sensitive Ecosystem Development Permit Areas.

blocks.text: Bolivar Heights Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Bolivar Park includes a two-acre fenced dog off-leash area east of the main parking lot, plus baseball fields, a field house and forest trails; parking is accessed from 115 Avenue.

The eastern part of Invergarry Park, around Wallace Drive and Surrey Road, holds the Invergarry Mountain Bike Park, with trails offering up to 25 metres of vertical and drops up to 3 metres on expert terrain.

blocks.text: Bolivar Heights Houses: development and new projects

items.t: The same update establishes a Central Business District, enables more transit-oriented development around SkyTrain stations, and plans additional parks and amenities.

Route 373 is the bus through Bolivar Heights: TransLink's timetable shows it running between Surrey Central Station and Guildford via Gateway Station and through 128 Street, 108 Avenue, Whalley Boulevard, 112 Avenue, 136 Street, 113 Avenue, Surrey Road, Wallace Drive and 116A Avenue.
Surrey Central Station, reached on the 373, is 150 metres from the City Centre library branch at 10350 University Drive and sits on the SkyTrain Expo Line.

blocks.text: Bolivar Heights Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check any lot backing onto the Bon Accord ravine for steep-slope and riparian constraints before planning an addition: the park protects the ravine and creek system, and Surrey's Steep Slope and Sensitive Ecosystem Development Permit Areas can require a permit.

Confirm a specific lot's floodplain status in the City's COSMOS mapping rather than from the neighbourhood's bluff position: Bolivar Heights sits on the upland above the Fraser River floodplain, and floodplain status is shown per address.

blocks.text: Bolivar Heights home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

65 houses sold in Bolivar Heights with a median price of $1,095,000 (the middle half sold between $1,010,000 and $1,205,000), taking a median of 32 days to sell at 95.8% of the last list price; 17% sold above list. They had a median $474 per square foot, a median year built of 1967 and a median lot of 7,553 square feet.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Bolivar Heights?
faq.a: 71, in the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board month-end figures for October 2026. Listings change every day; Jared can tell you what is available now.

faq.q: Is Bolivar Heights a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: Bolivar Heights houses sold at a sales ratio of 4% in October 2026, a buyers’ market on the reports’ scale (under 12% favours buyers, over 20% favours sellers).

faq.q: How many houses sold in Bolivar Heights from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 33 houses sold in Bolivar Heights over those 5 months, out of 464 in all of Surrey.

faq.q: Is Bolivar Heights part of the City Centre plan area?
faq.a: Yes. The City's City Centre Plan page states that the plan update now underway allows for growth in the Bolivar Heights area, including a mixed-use neighbourhood centre. That matters for a house buyer because the plan, updated after Council endorsed an Entertainment District proposal in October 2025, sets the direction for land use change around these established house streets.

faq.q: Which elementary schools are in Bolivar Heights itself?
faq.a: Two public schools are physically in the area: James Ardiel Elementary at 13751 112 Avenue and Surrey Traditional School at 13875 113 Avenue, both in the BC Ministry of Education list for School District 36.

faq.q: Does a SkyTrain station serve Bolivar Heights?
faq.a: No station is inside Bolivar Heights. The one TransLink route confirmed running through its streets is bus 373 between Surrey Central Station and Guildford, which passes Gateway Station on the Expo Line and runs via 112 Avenue, 136 Street, 113 Avenue, Surrey Road and Wallace Drive. Station access for a house here means a bus ride or drive to City Centre, not a walk to a platform.

faq.q: What is the ravine land in the middle of the area?
faq.a: It is Invergarry Park, which protects over 37.5 hectares of natural forest and riparian creek habitat in the Bon Accord ravine and creek system, with trail access from Gladstone Drive, Currie Drive, 111 Avenue, 114 Avenue and Surrey Road. Houses backing onto it sit beside protected creek habitat, which is why ravine-edge lots need a setback and permit check before any addition or rebuild.

faq.q: What did houses in Bolivar Heights sell for?
faq.a: From November 2025 to late October 2026, Bolivar Heights recorded 65 house sales at a median of $1,095,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Bolivar Heights?
faq.a: Typical time on the market was 32 days. At the median, sale prices were 95.8% of list, and 17% of sales closed above list (November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026).
